title: M/S Nikita Papers Ltd. v. U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. And Others
coram: Krishna Murari, J. & Mrs. Vijay Lakshmi, J.
disposition: Writ dismissed for want of prosecution; 27.11.2012 interim order vacated
headnote: On 27 November 2012 a Division Bench recorded the consumer's challenge to U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. giving the FY 2012-13 tariff retrospective effect from 1 October 2012, though it was published in the newspaper only on 23 October 2012. Counsel relied on Clause 3.8(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, Section 24(7) of the U.P. Electricity Reforms Act, 1999, and Regulation 139(2) of the UPERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2004 — each providing that a published tariff takes effect only seven days after publication — and on Section 62(6) of the Electricity Act, 2003. The petitioner did not dispute the Commission's tariff determination. The Court held that the matter required consideration, issued notice, and stayed disconnection on the impugned bill on conditions: payment at the new tariff from 1 November 2012; payment at the prior tariff for October 2012 and of any pre-October amount in the bill by 10 December 2012; and a bank guarantee for the October difference by that date, without prejudice, with automatic vacation on default and with late-payment surcharge and interest recoverable if the writ failed. On 25 April 2014 none appeared to press the writ even in the revised call. It was dismissed and the interim order vacated, without a construction of Clause 3.8 or Section 24(7).
facts:
M/S Nikita Papers Ltd. challenged a U.P. Power Corporation Ltd. bill applying the New Tariff for 2012-13 from 1 October 2012, though UPPCL published that tariff in the newspaper on 23 October 2012. The petitioner did not dispute the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission's determination; it objected only to retrospective operation. Counsel invoked Clause 3.8(a) of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, section 24(7) of the U.P. Electricity Reforms Act, 1999, and Regulation 139(2) of the UPERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2004 — each said to make a published tariff effective only seven days after publication (31 October 2012) — and section 62(6) of the Electricity Act, 2003 as a bar on recovering a tariff in excess of that determined under section 62.

On 27 November 2012 notice issued and disconnection on the impugned bill was stayed on payment and bank-guarantee conditions. On 25 April 2014 none appeared in the revised call; the writ was dismissed and the interim vacated.

holding_units.clause: 3.8(a) (tariff takes effect only after seven days from publication)
holding_units.topic: Interim stay of disconnection where a published tariff is given effect from a date before the seven-day publication window; writ later dismissed for want of prosecution
holding_units.question: Where a Commission-determined tariff is published on 23 October 2012, may the licensee apply it from 1 October 2012, or does Clause 3.8(a) confine its effect to seven days after publication?
holding_units.holding: Not decided on merits. The Court recorded the submission that publication on 23.10.2012 meant the New Tariff could take effect only on 31.10.2012, held that the matter required consideration, issued notice, and as interim relief directed that supply would not be disconnected on the impugned bill if: (i) from 1.11.2012 the petitioner paid at the New Tariff; (ii) for October 2012 it paid at the prior tariff by 10.12.2012; (iii) any pre-October amount in the bill was paid by that date; and (iv) the October difference was covered by a bank guarantee by that date, without prejudice. Default would vacate the stay automatically; if the writ were dismissed or the stay vacated, surcharge, interest and other late-payment charges would be recoverable from the guarantee and otherwise. The writ was later dismissed for want of prosecution without construing Clause 3.8.
holding_units.qualifier: Prima facie and interlocutory (27.11.2012, Satya Poot Mehrotra, J. and Het Singh Yadav, J.); the petition was dismissed on non-appearance on 25.4.2014 (Krishna Murari, J. and Mrs. Vijay Lakshmi, J.).
holding_units.flag: Two unnumbered order-sheets treated as paras 1 (27.11.2012 interlocutory) and 2 (25.4.2014 dismissal). Regulation 139(2) of the UPERC (Conduct of Business) Regulations, 2004 was invoked for the same seven-day rule and is not a catalog key. holding_units.clause: 24(7) (tariff comes into force after seven days from the last date of publication)
holding_units.topic: Section 24(7) seven-day publication rule invoked with Clause 3.8(a); not finally construed
holding_units.holding: The petitioner submitted that Section 24(7) required the New Tariff to come into force only after seven days from the last date of publication (23.10.2012), so it could not be given retrospective effect from 1.10.2012. The Court recorded the submission, held that the matter required consideration, and moulded interim billing accordingly. It did not finally construe Section 24(7).

holding_units.code: Article 226 — dismissal for want of prosecution
holding_units.topic: Writ dismissed when none appeared to press it; interim vacated
holding_units.holding: On 25.4.2014 the case was called in the revised list, none appeared to press the writ, it was dismissed, and the interim order, if any, stood vacated, without a final ruling on the retrospective-tariff bill.

principle_tags.application: Prima facie, and only as an interim billing arrangement, a tariff published on 23.10.2012 was not applied from 1.10.2012: the petitioner was to pay at the new rate from 1.11.2012 and at the prior rate for October, with a bank guarantee for the October difference. Clause 3.8(a) and Section 24(7) were not finally construed.

Disconnection on the impugned bill was stayed pending notice, subject to payment of the new tariff from 1.11.2012, payment at the prior tariff for October 2012 and of pre-October amounts by 10.12.2012, and a bank guarantee for the October difference, without prejudice and self-vacating on default.

None appearing to press the writ even in the revised call, it was dismissed on 25.4.2014 and the 27.11.2012 interim order stood vacated; the Clause 3.8 / Section 24(7) challenge was left unadjudicated.

not_decided.point: Whether the FY 2012-13 tariff published on 23.10.2012 could lawfully be given effect from 1.10.2012, or only from 31.10.2012 under Clause 3.8(a), Section 24(7) and Regulation 139(2)
not_decided.note: The 27.11.2012 view was that the matter required consideration; dismissal for non-appearance left the effective date unadjudicated.

not_decided.point: Whether Section 62(6) of the Electricity Act, 2003 independently barred recovery of the new tariff for October 2012
not_decided.note: Cited by the petitioner as a bar on recovering tariff in excess of that determined under Section 62; not applied. EA2003::62 is not a catalog key.

not_decided.point: Validity of the new tariff as determined by the U.P. Electricity Regulatory Commission
not_decided.note: The petitioner expressly did not dispute the Commission's determination.
